notes: Both numerals are outlined circles; the second is an outlined circle containing 52, written here as bare 52 because Unicode has no circled 52. Drawn as 3 cells with the middle one elided.

visual_anchor: D1 lower row, the single wide grey dash-outlined band filled with one long row of dots, immediately right of the last X:X cell of ㊺~52 and immediately left of the first X:X cell of 53~68, under the bracket labelled with two black-filled circles reading 6 and 52.
notes: STOP 1 | STOP 2 | Both numerals are BLACK-FILLED circles (white digits on black), unlike every other index on this diagram; the second is written here as bare 52 because Unicode has no black-circled 52. The band draws no X:X cell at all - one dashed grey region about three cell-widths wide - so its extent cannot be counted from cells and the 47 byte positions come from its own printed end numerals 6 and 52. Measured running position, counting from the diagram's first cell, is bytes 53 to 99.

visual_anchor: D1 lower row, the last three drawn cells of the diagram (white X:X, white dash-outlined ellipsis cell, white X:X), immediately right of the wide black-labelled band, under the bracket labelled 53~68.
notes: STOP 3 | Both numerals are outlined circles, written here as bare digits because Unicode has no circled 53 or 68. Drawn as 3 cells with the middle one elided; the printed range 53 to 68 is 16 bytes, but the measured running position, counting from the diagram's first cell, is bytes 100 to 115.

visual_anchor: D2, the two-nibble box in the left column below the heading "⑤: Split and Select memory setting", about one third down the page, with ⑤ printed directly above the box.
notes: Outlined circle. This box is a one-byte nibble legend, not a record, so byte 1 here is its own only byte; the same field is byte 5 of D1. Leader from the LEFT nibble runs to the LOWER label "0=Split OFF,1=Split ON"; leader from the RIGHT nibble runs to the UPPER label list "0=OFF*" / "1= ★1" / "2= ★2" / "3= ★3".

visual_anchor: D3, the two-nibble box in the left column below the heading "⑭: Duplex and Tone settings", lower half of the page, with ⑭ printed directly above the box.

visual_anchor: D4, the two-nibble box at the foot of the left column below the heading "⑮: Digital squelch setting", with ⑮ printed directly above the box and the numeral 0 printed in its second nibble.
notes: Outlined circle. One-byte nibble legend, not a record; the same field is byte 15 of D1. Leader from the LEFT nibble runs to the three lines "0=Digital squelch function OFF" / "1=Digital call sign squelch function ON (DSQL)" / "2=Digital code squelch function ON (CSQL)"; leader from the RIGHT nibble runs to "Fixed", printed above those three lines.
